subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should completed exec results with nonzero exit codes be treated as non-error results across agent, cron, UI, and delivery classifiers, or should nonzero-as-data be an opt-in exec mode?
rationale: The lower exec runtime already models normal nonzero exits as completed, but changing the shared classifier affects multiple product surfaces that use `isError` for failure accounting and delivery decisions.

options.title: Make normal nonzero exits completed
options.body: Update shared classification and cron/UI tests so normal exec exits 0-125 preserve output and exit code without setting tool-error state, while shell 126/127, timeout, signal, spawn, and denial paths remain failures.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in mode
options.body: Keep current failure accounting by default and add a documented exec option such as accepted exit codes for workflows that use semantic nonzero exits.

options.title: Document wrapper-only behavior
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document the shell wrapper workaround, accepting that cron jobs must encode semantic exit codes manually.

recommendation.title: Make normal nonzero exits completed
recommendation.body: Update shared classification and cron/UI tests so normal exec exits 0-125 preserve output and exit code without setting tool-error state, while shell 126/127, timeout, signal, spawn, and denial paths remain failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared classifier and related terminal-state PR history point to this owner for the cross-surface product boundary decision.
